title: lorentzian-causal-settling
description: A Boolean-valued settling whose cells are pairs of spacetime events and whose closure operator is causal transitivity; its settled fixed point is the full causal order generated by a seed relation of direct causal links, with the apex/void duality interpreting timelike/spacelike separation.

event-set.description: a finite or countable set E of spacetime events (Sorkin-style causal-set carrier)

seed-relation.description: a binary relation prec_0 subset of E x E of direct causal links - elementary timelike/null connections seeding the settling

cells.description: the cell space is E x E: each cell is an ordered pair (e1, e2) of events

initial-settling.description: v_0(e1, e2) = t if e1 prec_0 e2, else bottom - the knowledge-least valuation lifted by the seed links

closure-operator.description: causal transitivity T_caus(v)(e1, e3) = v(e1, e3) OR exists e2 . [v(e1, e2) AND v(e2, e3)] - the Boolean transitive-closure step, a special case of transitive closure

settled-fixed-point.description: v_kappa(e1, e2) = t iff a directed prec_0-path e1 -> e2 exists in E; the fixed point is the full causal order preceq on E generated by prec_0

closure-ordinal.description: the ordinal kappa at which causal transitivity stabilizes, classified by the four-regime dichotomy

kappa.description: ceil(log2 D) for finite E (D = longest directed path length); omega for a countable sprinkling; omega_1 or beyond for uncountable continuum causal sets

regime.description: strict (finite E, H^1 = 0, no NSC firings); scott-continuous (countably-infinite E, kappa = omega); aperiodic (uncountable causal sets in pathological cases, otherwise asymptotic-c)

apex-void-duality.description: the corpus apex/void cone duality read as Lorentzian timelike/spacelike separation

apex-timelike.description: a settled cell (v_kappa = t) is causally connected: a directed timelike-or-null curve runs e1 -> e2; apex generators record causal-acquisition events

void-spacelike.description: a permanently-bottom cell (neither (e1,e2) nor (e2,e1) settles) is spacelike separated: no causal curve connects e1 and e2 in either direction
